title: Ozone showed no clear link to the temperature slope of recorded bird richness in selected US surveys in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether a warmer survey start was linked to a larger decrease in recorded bird richness when ozone was higher. We joined the fixed USGS BBS 2025 release to EPA daily ozone for 2005-2024. Each route used one fixed nearby monitor. Four models used 13,180 surveys in eastern and western regions in two periods. Models controlled route-observer and state-year effects, survey timing, weather, and assistant status. Interaction slopes were -0.016, -0.167, +0.011, and -0.067 recorded taxa per 5 C and 10 ppb. All intervals corrected for four tests included zero. All 20 planned sensitivity intervals also included zero. This gives no clear evidence for the proposed interaction in the selected sample. Coverage retained 23-25 percent of western candidate runs and about 56 percent in the East. Only 18 exposure-matched candidates had both a start of at least 25 C and ozone of at least 70 ppb. The tests cannot resolve rare extremes, true species loss, or detection separately from birds present. Monitor distance, selected records, unmeasured prior weather, and changing habitat limit inference. A full fit repeat was byte-identical. The package includes code, fixed source hashes, derived records, exposure and numerical checks, figures, and offline instructions.
